title: Repeated common value auctions with asymmetric bidders
summary_en: In repeated common-value auctions — for example, repeated procurement rounds for the same type of good — bidders learn from each round about the underlying value. Virág studies how asymmetric bidders (e.g., an incumbent supplier with private information vs. a fresh entrant) play across repeated rounds, and characterises the conditions under which repetition mitigates the winner's curse vs. amplifies it. The paper bridges static common-value auction theory with dynamic, learning-driven auction settings relevant for procurement.
data_used: Theoretical paper in auction theory. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Useful theoretical input for the design of repeated public-procurement tenders in Hungary and the EU (KEFI multi-year framework agreements, EU framework procurement contracts): when the same buyers / sellers interact across rounds, asymmetric-information dynamics differ from one-shot auctions, and the paper characterises when repetition helps or hurts the buyer.
